thesis: Existence is not one undifferentiated status, and describing a thing does not instantiate it.
role: Develops realism of differences across physical, social and experienced reality.

ideas.statement: A real representation need not have a real object; institution-dependent entities can nevertheless impose real consequences.
Foundation, process and necessity arguments need explicit premises; nothingness is not an observed default.
Administrative categories distribute recognition and can conceal harms without making those harms unreal.
Branching identity exposes differences between numerical sameness and continuities relevant to care.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: The dragon, debt and vacuum illustrate distinct senses of reality.
A flame remains real without a permanent material core.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Historical philosophies are conceptual arguments, not anticipations of quantum experiments; mind-copying remains hypothetical.

audit.notes: Every unit read. Thought experiments distinguished from empirical evidence.
